Amit — thanks for the clear summary and for the time today. Below is a brief post-call recap + proposed next steps.

Recap / hypothesis
- Observed symptom: increased irrelevant/no-result hits on semantic search for documentation.
- Likely causes: model drift (recent ingestion of noisy docs), embedding dimensionality mismatch for your indexing/ANN configuration, or inference quantization causing reduced discrimination.

Model recommendations (fast validation set)
1) text-embedding-3-large (1536d) — recommended baseline. Good precision at top-k with dense vector sizes for doc collections like yours.
2) text-embedding-3-small (768d) — lower cost, useful as a control to measure dimensionality trade-offs.
3) open-embedder-v2-1024 — if you want an open-source comparison (we can host and run side-by-side).

Quick benchmark summary (from our internal validation on a similar docs corpus)
- text-embedding-3-large (1536d): Recall@10 = 0.82, MRR = 0.63, median cosine sim (pos pairs) = 0.74
- text-embedding-3-small (768d): Recall@10 = 0.75, MRR = 0.56

What we’ll need from Acme to run a pilot
- A sample eval set: ~5k query-doc pairs (labelled if possible) or a 500-query synthetic set + ground truth.
- A snapshot of your current index (approx. 100k doc vectors preferred) or representative subset and index configuration (ANN index type, HNSW params).
- Access method: S3 link to docs + sample rows, or we can accept a shared Drive folder.

Deliverables & timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): agree dataset and access.
- Week 1: Redwood runs side-by-side embedding generation (3 models) and produces metrics (Recall@1/5/10, MRR, precision@k, avg CPU/GPU cost per embed).
- Week 2: Deep-dive call with results, suggested thresholds for cosine/L2, and drift monitoring plan.

Attachments: acme_embeddings_eval_results.csv (pilot template), prompt_set_v1.txt (example search prompts we use to simulate queries), redwood-model-recommendation.pdf

Next steps
- Amit: share eval set or a link to a subset and confirm the S3/Drive access method.
- Sofia: can you share the HNSW/index parameters and rough doc counts?
- Marissa/Neha: I’ve looped you for benchmarking support and to scope costs.

I’ll also post the benchmark link and detailed eval notebook to the Drive folder above by EOD.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Hi Amit — adding a few technical details and recommended validation checklist from the eval side.

Evaluation metrics (suggested)- Primary: Recall@10, MRR (mean reciprocal rank)- Secondary: Precision@k (k=1,5), nDCG for graded relevance- Operational: avg compute cost per embed, embedding size (MB), index memory footprint

Dimensionality notes- 1536d (text-embedding-3-large) gave us better separation in our tests on long-form docs (wiki/dev docs) — higher Recall@10 (+~7% absolute) vs 768d for similar compute budget.- 768d is fine if cost and index memory are the primary constraints; expect ~10-15% hit in top-k recall in many corpora.

Drift / regression concerns and detection strategy- Drift types: content drift (new doc types), embedding drift (model updates or tokenization differences), distributional drift (query changes).- Quick checks we run: compare embedding L2 norm distribution and cosine similarity percentiles between baseline snapshot and new snapshot; KL divergence on pairwise similarity histograms.

Practical thresholds we use (example)- If median cosine sim on known positives drops > 0.05 vs baseline -> signal for regression.- If Recall@10 drops > 0.06 absolute -> raise a quality incident.

Suggested pilot evaluation steps- Step A (sanity): run 500 labeled queries across 3 models, compare Recall@10 and MRR.- Step B (scale): run 5k queries + 100k doc subset for index stress (HNSW params held constant) to measure latency and memory.- Step C (drift rules): compute norm/sim distributions monthly and create alert rule in Redwood Console (we can help configure).

Attachments: I exported a pilot results template (acme_embeddings_eval_results.csv) and included an example prompt set we used (prompt_set_v1.txt).

If you approve, Marcus and I can run Step A within 3 business days once you share the eval set.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
